title: Washing Machine Maintenance: Leveling, Hoses, and Leak-Prevention Upgrades
summary: This Old House demonstrates practical care and upgrades to reduce vibration, water leakage risk, and downtime for residential washing machines. The hosts begin by stressing that the unit should be level to minimize noise and movement during fast spinning, showing leveling legs and using a front-mounted level. They then discuss the water-supply side, noting back-wall hose connections, potential inline filters, and the risk of downstream shutoffs failing and clogging the inlet. The video contrasts rubber hoses with stainless steel braided hoses, explaining the higher durability of the latter and their lower burst risk. It surveys several leak-prevention approaches—manual and electronic shutoffs, and a floor-leak sensor—and explains a mechanical, non-electronic lever option that temporarily pressurizes the hoses for a limited window (two-and-a-half hours) and defaults to off, highlighting tradeoffs between simplicity and safety. The overall message is to combine proper leveling with robust hose fittings and reliable shut-off strategies to extend appliance life and reduce flood risk.

title: How to Repair a Garbage Disposer: Jam Clearing, Allen Wrench Access, and Torque Techniques
summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing and repairing a jammed garbage disposer. The video introduces disposer anatomy (flange, locking mechanism, splash guard), explains how waste travels into the disposer and how the dishwasher discharges into it, and then shows practical steps to clear a jam. When the motor hums due to an obstruction, the host uses the included Allen wrench to manually rotate the impeller, removes visible foreign objects with needle-nose pliers if needed, and, for higher torque, applies lever-based tools such as broomsticks and a pro wrench that can be fed through the splash guard to seat on the deck. After freeing the jam, the unit is tested to confirm smooth operation. The guidance emphasizes methodical diagnosis and controlled tool use rather than generic, off-camera procedures.

title: Kitchen Appliances Maintenance: Dishwashers, Refrigerators, Ice Makers, and Ovens (This Old House)
summary: This video presents a practical tour of common kitchen appliances and walks through practical maintenance tips to avoid service calls. It covers how a dishwasher operates (water inlet, heating, spray arms, filters, and float switch), loading and detergent considerations, and troubleshooting basics. It then examines refrigerator operation (evaporator coil and fan, condenser, and gasket care) with recommended cleaning methods. The ice-maker section discusses water-line reliability, self-piercing valves versus installing a shut-off, and the advantages of copper tubing. Finally, the segment on ranges and ovens distinguishes gas vs electric, coil vs smooth-top surfaces, and self-cleaning ovens, including what to clean (and what not to) and safety considerations around high-heat cycles and thermostats.

title: Installing a Heat Pump Water Heater | This Old House
summary: This Old House guides viewers through replacing an aging electric water heater with a modern heat-pump model. The video contrasts a traditional glass-lined tank with two 4,500-watt immersion elements to a heat-pump system that extracts heat from surrounding air with a 700-watt compressor and circulating refrigerant. It covers why the old unit loses efficiency due to mineral buildup and demonstrates the installation workflow: shutting off water and power, draining and removing the old heater, positioning the new unit, connecting cold and hot water lines (including a vacuum breaker and dip tube), routing condensate to a pump, wiring a 240V circuit, and choosing the hybrid mode for maximum energy savings. The host emphasizes safety steps, the need for a condensate drain, and the expected energy savings from the heat-pump approach, finishing with startup and normal operation settings.

title: How to Install Thermostatic Radiator Valves | This Old House
summary: This video provides a practical walkthrough for installing a thermostatic radiator valve (TRV) on an older radiator. It covers removing an existing valve assembly (including the valve body, nipple, and spud) with a spud wrench, preparing the new valve with thread sealant and wick, and using pipe dope on old piping. The demonstration then shows aligning and connecting the valve, routing a sensor through the radiator cover, securing the sensor with zip screws, installing a cover plate, and completing the final connections. The steps emphasize making a tight seal at the spud and careful handling of the sensor path within the radiator assembly.

title: Laundry Appliance Maintenance: Hoses, Venting, Lint, and Smart Diagnostics
summary: This episode of Ask This Old House presents practical, experience-based guidance for maintaining laundry appliances. Home expert Richie Isaacson outlines preventive measures to avoid floods and fires, focusing on washer hose health, proper loading, and detergent choices, followed by dryer maintenance. Key recommendations include upgrading to stainless steel braided washer hoses and replacing them every five years, avoiding overloading the washer, removing items from pockets, understanding top-load versus front-load designs, using high-efficiency detergent in HE machines, mitigating vibration with a dedicated pad and ensuring the unit is level, and rigorous dryer lint and vent maintenance. The segment also compares venting options (vinyl, aluminum, and solid pipe), notes that solid pipe is preferred by manufacturers, and emphasizes annual vent cleaning. The host team closes with a nod to emerging smart-diagnosis tools that acoustically or app-diagnose issues, illustrated by a dryer vent blockage detected via an app and a washer’s audible-diagnosis feature.

title: Understanding New Water Heater Regulations: Insulation, Venting, and Efficiency Options
summary: The video presents a concise explainer of newer water heater standards that affect only new installations. It covers how insulation requirements for small gas units are increasing to reduce standby energy loss, clarifies which units qualify as “condensing” with venting changes away from chimney exhaust, and explains electric storage limits, while highlighting the growing role of hybrid heat-pump models and on-demand systems. It also emphasizes practical constraints in tight spaces (closets, basements), the need to rework chimneys for venting, and the rule that existing water heaters are not required to be replaced until their next cycle. The host notes estimated energy savings, cost and size premiums, and typical lifespans to contextualize choosing a compliant upgrade when replacing a unit.

title: How to Maintain a Furnace | Ask This Old House
summary: This Old House’s short guide explains essential furnace maintenance routines for a home system. It covers the rationale for annual service (ideally in fall), what a homeowner can do (notably inspecting and replacing the air filter with attention to orientation), and what a professional HVAC technician checks (combustion air quality, safety sensors, and efficiency). The host contrasts older furnaces that draw combustion air from inside with modern units that may pull air from outside, and emphasizes keeping combustion areas clear of dust and lint. The video closes by noting typical efficiency differences between older (~81–82%) and modern furnaces (up to ~97%), and underscores that proper maintenance can extend furnace life to about 20 years.

title: Relocating a Washer/Dryer to a First-Floor Bathroom Closet (Ask This Old House)
summary: This This Old House episode documents a couple’s plan to relocate their laundry from a basement/ cellar to a first-floor bathroom closet to support aging in place and eliminate stairs. The project team evaluates the closet size, plumbing, and vent routing; discusses electrical service upgrades (upgrading to 200A with dedicated circuits for a washer and a dryer); coordinates a trades team (electrician and carpenter); plans framing, door repositioning, and finish carpentry to create a neat, accessible laundry niche. The workflow covers wiring runs through the ceiling, completing a rough-in for new 20A/120V and 30A/240V circuits, venting, water shutoffs, a valve box, and a planning path that keeps existing appliances functional during the remodel. The episode also highlights practical considerations for aging-in-place design, including door clearances, thresholds, and accessible controls, culminating in a demonstration of the new stacked washer-dryer installation.
